analysis: Avalanche and bit independence on 2000 random 16-byte keys. At the BLAKE2b-64 noise floor (mean bias 0.0089, max 0.045, BIC 0.11) - QG-LS with a reverse pass (1, 2 or 4 forward passes), QG-ISO p2+rev, QG-NIMINV p1/p2+rev, MX64. QG-ARP p2+rev also has ideal per-bit flip rates (max bias 0.043) but perfectly correlated bit changes (BIC 1.0). Failing - every forward-only variant (max bias 0.5, mean 0.09-0.10), FNV-1a-64 (mean 0.098, max 0.5, 1688 cells above 0.1), the T-function quasigroups AFF and ALP (mean 0.39 and 0.34) and the GF(2)-affine XOR and CRC32 (mean 0.5).
assumptions: 2000 random 16-byte keys (seeded); all 128 input bits flipped
bias = |P(output bit flips) - 1/2|; with 2000 keys the sampling standard deviation per cell is about 0.011, so BLAKE2b's values estimate the noise floor
falsification: H-C18-1: a difference > 0.01 in mean or maximal bias. H-C18-2: a structured quasigroup with maximal bias <= that of QG-LS p2+rev. H-C18-3a: NIMINV mean bias above FNV-1a's. H-C18-5: a forward-only variant with maximal bias < 0.5.

QG-ARP p2+rev also has ideal per-bit flip rates (max bias 0.043) but perfectly correlated bit changes (BIC 1.0). Failing - every forward-only variant (max bias 0.5, mean 0.09-0.10), FNV-1a-64 (mean 0.098, max 0.5, 1688 cells above 0.1), the T-function quasigroups AFF and ALP (mean 0.39 and 0.34) and the GF(2)-affine XOR and CRC32 (mean 0.5).

hypothesis: H-C18-1 (bold): QG-LS with 2 passes and a reverse pass has mean and maximal avalanche bias within 0.01 of BLAKE2b-64. H-C18-2: every structured quasigroup (AFF, XOR, ARP, ALP) is worse than the random Latin square on maximal avalanche bias. H-C18-3a (bold): the nimber inversion quasigroup (NIMINV, 2 passes + reverse) has avalanche at least as good as FNV-1a-64. H-C18-5 (from Theorem 2): every forward-only variant has maximal bias 0.5.
methodology: For each hash and input bit, flip the bit in all keys and record which output bits change; report mean flip rate, mean and maximal bias, cells with bias > 0.1, deterministic cells, and the maximal/mean absolute correlation between output-bit changes (bit independence).
question: How close to an ideal 64-bit mixer are e-transformation hashes over the seven quasigroups, with 1, 2 or 4 passes and with or without a reverse pass?
